name: Chemical energetics enthalpy changes and calorimetry

questions.q: What term defines the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is formed from its constituent elements in their standard states under standard conditions?
a: Standard enthalpy change of formation (Delta H_f)
Standard enthalpy change of combustion
Standard enthalpy change of neutralization
Standard enthalpy change of atomization

questions.q: How is the standard enthalpy change of combustion (Delta H_c) defined?
a: The energy released when one mole of water is produced from its elements
The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is burned completely in excess oxygen under standard conditions
The energy required to melt one mole of a solid compound
The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed

questions.q: According to Hess's Law, what is the fundamental principle regarding enthalpy changes in chemical reactions?
a: Enthalpy change depends on the intermediate reaction steps taken
Enthalpy change is always zero for spontaneous processes
The total enthalpy change of a chemical reaction is independent of the pathway between initial and final states
Enthalpy change increases with temperature exponentially

questions.q: What formula is used to calculate the heat energy change (q) during a calorimetry experiment involving a solution?
a: q = m x c x Delta T
q = n x Delta H
q = P x V
q = C x Delta T squared

questions.q: What is the standard enthalpy change of neutralization defined as?
a: The enthalpy change when one mole of water is formed by the reaction of an acid and an alkali under standard conditions
The energy released when an acid dissolves in water
The enthalpy change when one mole of a salt is precipitated
The energy required to dissociate a weak acid

questions.q: What term represents the energy required to break one mole of a specific covalent bond in gaseous molecules, averaged over a range of similar compounds?
a: Lattice energy
Mean bond enthalpy / Bond dissociation energy
Electron affinity
Enthalpy of vaporization

questions.q: Which of the following represents an exothermic reaction process?
a: Melting of ice
Boiling of liquid water
Combustion of methane in oxygen
Dissolving ammonium nitrate in water

questions.q: What is the standard enthalpy change of atomization defined as?
a: The energy released when gaseous atoms combine to form a solid lattice
The enthalpy change when one mole of electrons is added to gaseous atoms
The energy required to convert a liquid into a gas at boiling point
The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from the element in its standard state under standard conditions

questions.q: What is the standard enthalpy change of formation for any element in its standard state (e.g., O<sub>2</sub> gas, C graphite)?
a: Zero
Positive infinity
Negative one hundred kilojoules per mole
Variable depending on pressure

questions.q: Using bond enthalpies, how is the approximate enthalpy change of a reaction (Delta H) calculated?
a: Sum of bonds formed minus sum of bonds broken
Sum of bonds broken minus sum of bonds formed
Total reactant enthalpy multiplied by product enthalpy
Sum of all standard formation enthalpies

questions.q: What type of reaction is characterized by a negative value of Delta H and releases thermal energy to the surroundings?
a: Endothermic reaction
Photochemical reaction
Exothermic reaction
Isothermal reaction

questions.q: What does Born-Haber cycle construction utilize to determine the lattice energy of an ionic compound?
a: Faraday's laws of electrolysis
Rate equations and activation energy
Ideal gas law constants
Hess's Law combining enthalpy changes such as atomization, ionization, electron affinity, and formation

questions.q: What is the first electron affinity of an atom defined as?
a: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous 1- ions is formed by adding one mole of electrons to one mole of gaseous atoms
The energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom
The enthalpy change when a solid salt dissolves in water
The energy released when two atoms form a covalent bond

questions.q: What term describes the enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous ions dissolves in sufficient water to form an infinitely dilute solution?
a: Enthalpy of lattice formation
Enthalpy of hydration
Enthalpy of solution
Enthalpy of atomization

questions.q: What is the relationship between the enthalpy of solution (Delta H_sol), lattice energy (Delta H_lattice), and hydration enthalpies (Delta H_hyd) of ions?
a: Delta H_sol equals Delta H_lattice plus sum of Delta H_hyd
Delta H_sol equals Delta H_hyd minus Delta H_lattice
Delta H_sol equals sum of Delta H_hyd minus Delta H_lattice
Delta H_sol equals Delta H_lattice multiplied by Delta H_hyd

questions.q: Why is the second electron affinity of oxygen (forming O<sup>2-</sup> from O<sup>-</sup>) an endothermic process?
a: Oxygen atoms are too heavy to accept electrons
Energy is absorbed because electrons repel each other when added to a negatively charged ion
Electrons possess positive mass charge
The nucleus repels incoming electrons completely

questions.q: What standard condition for temperature is used in thermochemical measurements?
a: 298 Kelvin (25 degrees Celsius)
273 Kelvin (0 degrees Celsius)
373 Kelvin (100 degrees Celsius)
298 degrees Celsius

questions.q: Which of the following factors increases the magnitude of lattice energy in ionic crystals?
a: Larger ionic radii and smaller charges
Higher ionic charges and smaller ionic radii
Lower melting points and higher volatility
Increased distance between cations and anions

questions.q: What does a positive sign for the enthalpy change of a reaction (Delta H > 0) signify?
a: The reaction is spontaneous at all temperatures
The reaction releases heat to the surroundings
The reaction is endothermic, absorbing heat from the surroundings
The reaction rate is extremely fast

questions.q: When calculating enthalpy change from experimental calorimetry data where 50.0 cm<sup>3</sup> of acid reacts with 50.0 cm<sup>3</sup> of alkali, what mass (m) is typically used in q = m c Delta T assuming dilute aqueous solutions?
a: 50.0 grams
25.0 grams
0.100 kilograms
100.0 grams (total volume assuming density of water is 1.0 g per cm cubed)

questions.q: What is the standard pressure condition used in thermochemistry?
a: 100 kilopascals (1 bar)
1 atmosphere (101.3 kPa)
10 kilopascals
500 kilopascals

questions.q: Which of the following processes has a standard enthalpy change of reaction that is equal to the standard enthalpy of formation of the product?
a: Combustion of carbon monoxide to form carbon dioxide
Formation of one mole of liquid water from hydrogen gas and oxygen gas
Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate
Neutralization of hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide

questions.q: Why are bond enthalpy values calculated from tables sometimes slightly different from actual experimental reaction enthalpy changes?
a: Bond enthalpies are only valid for ionic crystals
Mean bond enthalpies are averaged values derived from a range of different chemical environments, whereas actual bond energies vary slightly depending on molecular structure
Experimental reactions always lose 50 percent of energy as light
Bond enthalpies ignore temperature effects entirely

questions.q: What is the enthalpy change of solution defined as?
a: The energy required to melt a solid solute
The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance dissolves in water to form a saturated solution
The heat released when a gas dissolves under pressure
The enthalpy change when one mole of a solute is dissolved in sufficient solvent to form an infinitely dilute solution

questions.q: What experimental error is typically the primary cause of inaccurate enthalpy of combustion values measured using a simple spirit burner and copper calorimeter?
a: Heat loss to the surrounding atmosphere and incomplete combustion of the fuel
Evaporation of the metal calorimeter
Using too much water in the beaker
Measuring temperature in Fahrenheit instead of Celsius

questions.q: How does the hydration enthalpy of Group 2 metal cations change down the group from magnesium to barium?
a: Hydration enthalpy increases in magnitude
Hydration enthalpy decreases in magnitude (becomes less exothermic) as ionic radius increases
Hydration enthalpy remains completely constant
Hydration enthalpy becomes positive

questions.q: What does Hess's Law allow chemists to determine indirectly?
a: The exact speed of electrons in atomic orbitals
The exact mass of subatomic particles
Enthalpy changes that cannot be measured directly by direct experiment
The absolute enthalpy of a single isolated substance

questions.q: Which of the following equations correctly defines the standard enthalpy change of formation of liquid ethanol (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH)?
a: 2C (graphite) + 3H<sub>2</sub> (g) + 0.5O<sub>2</sub> (g) -> C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (l)
C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> (g) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l) -> C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (l)
2CO<sub>2</sub> (g) + 3H<sub>2</sub>O (l) -> C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (l) + 3O<sub>2</sub> (g)
C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (l) + 3O<sub>2</sub> (g) -> 2CO<sub>2</sub> (g) + 3H<sub>2</sub>O (l)

questions.q: What is the primary reason why lattice enthalpies calculated theoretically using electrostatic point-charge models sometimes differ from experimental Born-Haber cycle values for transition metal compounds?
a: Presence of significant covalent character due to polarization of anions by cations
Transition metals do not form ionic lattices
Experimental values ignore temperature
Theoretical models assume zero ionic charge

questions.q: What is indicated if the calculated standard enthalpy change of a reaction (Delta H) is negative?
a: The products have higher total enthalpy than the reactants
The products have lower total enthalpy than the reactants, and the reaction is exothermic
The reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings
The activation energy is zero

questions.q: Which of the following experimental setups is used to measure the enthalpy of neutralization accurately?
a: A metal crucible heated with a Bunsen burner
A bomb calorimeter under high pressure oxygen
An insulated polystyrene cup calorimeter with a thermometer and lid
An electrolytic cell connected to a DC power supply

questions.q: What is the standard state physical form of bromine at 298 Kelvin and 100 kilopascals?
a: Gas
Solid crystal
Aqueous solution
Liquid

questions.q: What term defines the total internal energy plus the product of pressure and volume (U + PV) of a thermodynamic system?
a: Enthalpy
Entropy
Gibbs free energy
Activation energy

questions.q: How does an increase in temperature affect the rate of an exothermic reaction according to collision theory?
a: Reaction rate decreases because equilibrium shifts left
Reaction rate increases because more reactant particles possess kinetic energy equal to or greater than the activation energy, increasing successful collision frequency
Reaction rate remains constant
Activation energy decreases

questions.q: Which of the following enthalpy changes is always endothermic (positive value)?
a: Enthalpy of combustion
Enthalpy of hydration
First ionization energy
Enthalpy of neutralization

questions.q: What is represented by the activation energy (E_a) on an enthalpy profile diagram?
a: The overall enthalpy change of the reaction
The total energy of the products
The average bond energy of reactants
The minimum energy colliding particles must possess to initiate a chemical reaction
